questions.question: When using a formula indicator, what happens by default if one of the contributing indicators has no score for a collection period?

options.text: The formula calculates using zero for the null indicator
The formula indicator returns no score
The formula raises an error in the job log
The formula skips that indicator and calculates with remaining values

explanation.correct: If one of the indicators in a formula has no score, by default the formula is not calculated and the formula indicator returns no score.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Zero is not substituted automatically; the formula simply doesn't calculate unless 'Allow formula component to be null' is enabled.
No error is raised; the formula indicator simply returns null/no score.
The formula does not automatically skip null indicators; special handling must be configured using 'Allow formula component to be null'.

source.excerpt: If one of those indicators has no score, by default the formula is not calculated and the formula indicator returns no score.

questions.question: Which checkbox must be selected on a formula indicator to enable handling of null scores from contributing indicators?

options.text: Allow formula component to be null

explanation.correct: Select 'Allow formula component to be null' on the formula indicator to enable calculation even when a contributing indicator has no score.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This is not a valid PA field name; the correct option is 'Allow formula component to be null'.
There is no 'Skip null indicators' checkbox; you must use 'Allow formula component to be null'.
This is not a valid PA field name; the correct option is 'Allow formula component to be null'.

source.excerpt: Select Allow formula component to be null.

questions.question: A PA administrator manually enters scores for an automated indicator in the Scoresheet. What happens when the next data collection job runs?

options.text: The manually entered scores are preserved and the job skips those periods
The manually entered scores are overwritten by the job
The job fails with a conflict error
The job merges the manual and collected scores

explanation.correct: You can manually overwrite data that a job collected. However, the next time a job runs that collects this data, the manually entered data is overwritten in turn.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Manual scores are not preserved; they are overwritten by the next collection job.
No conflict error occurs; the job simply overwrites the manual data.
There is no merge functionality; the job completely overwrites previously entered data.

source.excerpt: You can manually overwrite data that a job collected. However, the next time that a job is run that collects this data, the manually entered data is overwritten in turn.

questions.question: Which two roles can manually add or edit indicator scores in the PA Scoresheet? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: The roles pa_contributor, pa_admin, pa_power_user, or admin can manually add or edit indicator scores in the Scoresheet.

wrongAnswers.explanation: pa_viewer only provides read access to PA data and cannot modify scores.
The itil role is for IT Service Management and does not grant PA score editing permissions.

source.excerpt: Role required: pa_contributor, pa_admin, pa_power_user, or admin

questions.question: Which type of indicator CANNOT have its scores manually edited in the Scoresheet?

explanation.correct: You cannot edit scores manually for formula indicators because their scores are calculated from other indicators.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Automated indicators can have scores manually edited, though they will be overwritten by the next job.
Manual indicators are specifically designed for manual score entry.
External indicators can have their scores managed through various methods including manual entry.

source.excerpt: You cannot edit scores manually for formula indicators.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of KPI Composer in Performance Analytics?

options.text: To automatically collect indicator scores from tables
To align performance measurement strategy with business goals before implementation
To create dashboard widgets and visualizations
To schedule and run data collection jobs

explanation.correct: KPI Composer helps elicit performance management requirements and drive stakeholder alignment by ensuring that goals, outcomes, and deliverables are aligned before implementers begin technical work.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Data collection is handled by data collector jobs, not KPI Composer.
While KPI Composer includes dashboard design capabilities, its primary purpose is strategic alignment, not widget creation.
Job scheduling is managed through PA Admin Console and data collector settings, not KPI Composer.

source.excerpt: KPI Composer ensures that your performance management strategy aligns with business goals and has support from executive sponsors.

questions.question: Which three tabs are included in a KPI Composer project UI? (Choose three.)

explanation.correct: KPI Composer project UI has four tabs: Analysis, Dashboard Design, Data Definition, and Review. The first three are all part of the design process.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Job Scheduling is not a tab in KPI Composer; job scheduling is done through PA Admin Console.
Score Collection is not a KPI Composer tab; the fourth tab is Review, which validates the design.

source.excerpt: The KPI Composer project UI provides you with a sequence of four tabs, each corresponding to a phase in your project: Analysis, Dashboard Design, Data Definition, Review

questions.question: Which role is required to create a new KPI Composer project?

explanation.correct: The role sn_kpi_composer.user, sn_kpi_composer.admin, or admin is required to create a new KPI Composer project.

wrongAnswers.explanation: pa_viewer provides read-only access to PA data and does not include KPI Composer permissions.
pa_contributor allows score entry but does not include KPI Composer project creation permissions.
The itil role is for IT Service Management and does not provide KPI Composer access.

questions.question: What is the difference between a user with the sn_kpi_composer.admin role and one with sn_kpi_composer.user role regarding PA integration?

options.text: Admin can view more projects than user
Admin can associate definitions with actual Performance Analytics indicators and breakdowns
Admin can create more projects than user
Admin has access to different tabs in KPI Composer

explanation.correct: A KPI Composer admin has full access to all projects AND can associate indicator and breakdown definitions with actual Performance Analytics indicators and breakdowns. A user role cannot perform this association.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The key difference is the ability to link to PA entities, not just project visibility.
Both roles can create projects; the difference is in PA integration capabilities.
Both roles access the same tabs; the difference is in PA entity association capabilities.

source.excerpt: A KPI Composer user does not automatically have access to all projects and cannot associate indicator or breakdown definitions with actual Performance Analytics entities.

questions.question: In the Scoresheet, what does the percentage bar above each column of breakdown scores indicate?

options.text: The percentage of the target achieved
The percentage of breakdown elements that contain scores
The percentage change from the previous period
The percentage of manual vs automated scores

explanation.correct: A percentage bar above each column of scores indicates the percentage of breakdown elements that contain scores. A value of 0 counts as a score; only the absence of any value counts as empty.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The percentage bar shows score completeness, not target achievement.
Change from previous period would be shown differently, not as a completeness bar.
The bar indicates score presence, not the source type of scores.

source.excerpt: A percentage bar above each column of scores indicates the percentage of breakdown elements that contain scores. A value of 0 counts as a score; only the absence of any value counts as empty.

questions.question: An administrator wants to calculate the main score for an indicator by totaling all breakdown element scores. Which Scoresheet feature should they use?

explanation.correct: Click Aggregate scores in the Scoresheet to choose whether to use Sum or Average of a specific breakdown to calculate the main scores for the indicator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Calculate Total is not a valid Scoresheet option; use Aggregate scores.
Sum Elements is not a valid option; Aggregate scores provides Sum and Average options.
Consolidate Breakdowns is not a valid feature; Aggregate scores handles this.

source.excerpt: Click Aggregate scores. Choose whether you want to use the Sum or the Average of a specific breakdown to calculate the main scores for the indicator.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding auditing of manual score changes in Performance Analytics?

options.text: All manual changes are automatically audited
Manual changes are audited only when enabled at the table level
Manual scoresheet changes are NOT audited, even when auditing is enabled
Only admin changes to scores are audited

explanation.correct: Auditing does not track manual changes to the scoresheet. Manual inserts, updates, and deletions are not audited, even when auditing is enabled at the Dictionary level for all pa_scores tables.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Manual scoresheet changes are explicitly excluded from auditing.
Even with table-level auditing enabled, scoresheet changes are not tracked.
No manual changes are audited regardless of the user's role.

source.excerpt: Auditing does not track manual changes to the scoresheet. Manual inserts, updates, and deletions are not audited, even when auditing is enabled at the Dictionary level for all pa_scores tables.

questions.question: Which two levels of access can be granted when sharing a KPI Composer project? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: When sharing a KPI Composer project, you can grant either Can view (read-only) or Can edit (read-write) access.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Full admin access requires the sn_kpi_composer.admin role, not project sharing.
Delete access is not a sharing option; deletion is controlled by ownership and admin roles.

source.excerpt: Select either Can view or Can edit access.

questions.question: Where is KPI Composer available for download?

explanation.correct: KPI Composer is available on the ServiceNow Store. Navigate to System Applications > Search ServiceNow Store to find and download it.

wrongAnswers.explanation: KPI Composer is an application from the Store, not an update set.
The PA module doesn't host KPI Composer for download; it's a Store application.
ServiceNow Community is for discussions, not application downloads.

source.excerpt: KPI Composer is available on the ServiceNow Store. Navigate to System Applications > Search ServiceNow Store

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Review tab in a KPI Composer project?

options.text: To verify design components and generate implementation tasks

explanation.correct: In the Review phase, you verify the design components in your project, run a system definition health check, and generate a task list for implementing the project in Performance Analytics.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Indicator definitions are created in the Data Definition tab.
Dashboard mock-ups are created in the Dashboard Design tab.
Breakdown sources are part of the Analysis and Data Definition phases.

source.excerpt: Review: In this phase, verify the design components in your project, run a system definition health check, and generate a task list for implementing the project in Performance Analytics.

questions.question: In the PA architecture, what must match between an indicator and its indicator source for data collection to work?

explanation.correct: The frequencies of the indicator and the indicator source must match. An indicator frequency is the frequency for which data is collected for an indicator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The table is defined on the indicator source; the indicator inherits it.
Breakdown configuration is separate from the indicator-source relationship.
Dashboard assignment is unrelated to data collection.

questions.question: An indicator has additional conditions beyond those inherited from its indicator source. When does the system evaluate these additional conditions?

options.text: When the indicator source is created
During the map/reduce function when processing each record
When the data collection job is scheduled

explanation.correct: During the map/reduce processing of each record, the system executes or evaluates any scripts and validates indicator conditions, including additional conditions set on the indicator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Additional conditions are evaluated at collection time, not source creation time.
Additional conditions filter during collection, not at render time.
Conditions are evaluated during job execution, not scheduling.

questions.question: What happens when a data collection job encounters an indicator with a null score value?

options.text: The null value is stored as zero
The null value is logged and a configured 'Value when nil' is stored
The indicator is skipped for that collection period
An error is logged and the job continues

explanation.correct: Any indicator with a null value is logged, and the configured 'Value when nil' is stored as the score. The log shows entries like: Stored 'Value when nil': 0.0 as score for indicator.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Zero is not automatically used; the 'Value when nil' setting determines the stored value.
The indicator is not skipped; a nil value is stored.
It is not treated as an error.

questions.question: Which two fields does an indicator source contain? (Choose two.)

options.text: Reference to a business process table
Conditions for filtering records of the table

explanation.correct: Indicator sources contain a reference to a business process table, a reference to a field with unique values, conditions for filtering records, and the indicator frequency.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dashboard widget configuration is not part of an indicator source.
Breakdown matrix settings are configured separately, not on indicator sources.

questions.question: An administrator sets up a formula indicator using two contributing indicators. During data collection, one contributing indicator has no score for March. What should the administrator configure to allow the formula to calculate using zero instead?

options.text: Set 'Value when nil' to 0 on the contributing indicator
Enable 'Allow formula component to be null' on the formula indicator
Configure a default score on the indicator source
Set the formula to use COALESCE function

explanation.correct: The 'Allow formula component to be null' checkbox must be selected on the formula indicator to handle null contributing scores. When enabled, null values are treated as zero in the calculation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Value when nil affects the contributing indicator's own collection, not formula behavior.
Default scores on indicator sources don't affect formula null handling.
COALESCE is not a PA formula configuration option.
